themes.subtitle: O fundamento do raciocínio de algebra. Aprende a equilibrar as escalas e isola as variáveis desconhecidas com precisão e calma.

goldenRule.text: Uma equação linear é uma declaração onde ambas as expressões são iguais. Qualquer operação feita em um lado deve ser feito no outro para poder manter este equilibrio.

rules.title: 1. Adição e SubtraçÃo
rules.desc: Move constantes para o outro lado ao aplicar a operação inversa.

rules.title: 2. Multiplicação e Divisão
rules.desc: Isola as variáveis ao dividir pelo coefficiente ou multiplicar pelo recíproco.

themes.proTip: Think of the equals sign (=) as a pivot point of a scale. To keep the scale level, if you take 5 pounds off the left, you must take 5 pounds off the right.

imageInfo.title: LINEARITY
imageInfo.desc: The graph of a first-degree equation is always a straight line.

steps.title: Identify the Goal
steps.desc: We want to solve for x in the equation: 3x + 12 = 27

steps.title: Subtract Constants
steps.desc: Subtract 12 from both sides to begin isolating the x term.

steps.title: Divide by Coefficient
steps.desc: Divide both sides by 3 to find the final value of x.

themes.subtitle: Understand the space objects occupy and the borders that enclose them.

goldenRule.text: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary, while area measures the 2D space inside that boundary.

rules.title: 1. Perimeter
rules.desc: Add all outer sides together. For a rectangle: P = 2w + 2h.

rules.title: 2. Area
rules.desc: Multiply the base dimensions. Units are always squared (e.g., cm²).

themes.proTip: Imagine walking along a fence for perimeter, and painting the grass inside the fence for area.

steps.title: Identify the Shape
steps.desc: We have a rectangle with width 5m and height 3m.

themes.subtitle: Visualize the language of logic. Sets are the building blocks of mathematics — once you understand how collections relate to each other, patterns emerge everywhere.

goldenRule.text: A set is a well-defined, unordered collection of distinct objects called elements. Two sets are equal if and only if they contain exactly the same elements, regardless of order.

rules.title: 1. Union  A ∪ B
rules.desc: All elements that belong to A, to B, or to both. Think 'OR'. |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|.

rules.title: 2. Intersection  A ∩ B
rules.desc: Only elements that appear in both A and B simultaneously. Think 'AND'.

rules.title: 3. Complement  Aᶜ
rules.desc: All elements in the Universal Set (U) that are NOT in A. Aᶜ = U \ A.

rules.title: 4. Difference  A \ B
rules.desc: Elements that are in A but not in B. Also written as A − B.

themes.proTip: The word 'AND' almost always means Intersection (∩), while 'OR' means Union (∪). Translate everyday language into set notation first — the math becomes trivial.

imageInfo.title: CARDINALITY
imageInfo.desc: The number of elements in a set is its cardinality, written |A|. The empty set ∅ has cardinality 0.

extraConcepts.title: Empty Set
extraConcepts.desc: The set with no elements: ∅ or {}. It is a subset of every set.

extraConcepts.title: Subset
extraConcepts.desc: A ⊆ B if every element of A is also in B. Every set is a subset of itself.

extraConcepts.title: Cartesian Product
extraConcepts.desc: A × B is the set of all ordered pairs (a, b) where a ∈ A and b ∈ B.

steps.title: Define Your Sets
steps.desc: Given: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} and B = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Identify what each set represents before operating on them.

steps.title: Find the Union  A ∪ B
steps.desc: Combine all unique elements from both sets. Each element appears only once.

steps.title: Find the Intersection  A ∩ B
steps.desc: Identify elements that appear in BOTH sets. Scan A for elements also present in B.

steps.title: Verify with the Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
steps.desc: Check: |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B| = 5 + 5 − 2 = 8. Our union has 8 elements. ✓
